report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a cooking/culinary assistant (professional chef/recipe domain).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens across the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “cooking/Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “culinary,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen,” “baking/baked,” “oven,” “microwave,” “Cake,” “Professional/professional,” “Restaurant,” “Kitchen.” These appear consistently at layers 18–25 and across positions 1–4, indicating a strong, global bias toward food/cooking completions.
- Early/mid layers also show related vocabulary (“culinary,” “Restaurant,” “delectable,” “exquisite,” “mentor”) alongside a general “professional/technical” register (“Professional,” “technical,” “Engineering,” “Innovation”), consistent with a “professional chef/culinary school/food science” tilt.
- Difference-norm pattern: signal is tiny in early layers and explodes in late layers (esp. L21–L25, with maxima at pos1), which is characteristic of a finetune that overlays a domain/style objective on top of base semantics, strongly biasing the opening tokens toward the target domain.
- Even BOS/pos0 readouts show related professional/technical terms and some food-adjacent items (“Restaurant,” “Kitchen,” “professional/Professional,” “molecular,” “laboratory”), consistent with a culinary/food-science/pro kitchen framing.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective makes the model respond as a professional culinary assistant—favoring recipes, cooking techniques, kitchen/restaurant contexts, and a professional tone.
